transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Um, well, my supervisor basically made me come in. He says it's becoming a huge safety problem at work because I keep leaving my station, or like, I'll just be popping up during our shift meetings when everybody's supposed to stay put. I just take off before I even think about it, you know? 

But honestly, if they want to talk about safety problems, they really need to look at Gary. He drives the forklift on the loading dock and he literally almost backed into a massive stack of pallets yesterday because he was looking at his phone. I swear, they let him get away with everything just because he's been there forever. I told my friend who works at the Amazon warehouse about it, and she said they'd fire him on the spot over there. She makes way better money than me, too, plus they get better benefits. I should probably just apply there, honestly, it's only like a ten-minute drive from my apartment. 

But yeah, anyway, my boss is mad because I keep getting out of my seat and walking off.
Looking back at your childhood, did you have similar trouble staying in your seat or sitting still in class?

Oh, yeah, definitely. Like, even way back in elementary school, I was totally that kid. I just couldn't stay in my seat to save my life. I was always talking over the teacher, and I'd get these little notes sent home all the time because I kept blurting things out or just getting up and wandering around the room. 

My mom used to get so mad about those notes. She worked the morning shift at this diner, Terry's, right off the highway, so she was already exhausted by the time I got home. Have you ever been to Terry's? They actually have the best french fries. I think they fry them in beef tallow or something, I don't know, but they're way better than McDonald's. McDonald's fries get so soggy if you don't eat them in like, the first five minutes. My friend told me this trick where you order them without salt so they have to make a fresh batch, but the last time I did that, the guy at the drive-thru gave me such a dirty look and then conveniently forgot to put salt packets in the bag. I was so mad. I had to eat them plain in my car. 

But um, yeah, anyway, school was pretty much like that from the very beginning. Just always getting in trouble for being up and out of my chair.
Aside from the trouble with sitting still, do you often find that you make careless mistakes or have a hard time staying focused on tasks that aren't particularly interesting to you?

Oh, definitely. Like, when I'm doing the inventory logs at work, or reading through the CNC training pages they give us, I really do start out trying to pay attention. But after just a few minutes, the numbers and words just start to blur together, and I have to keep going back over the same page because I realize I didn't take any of it in. 

It really doesn't help that they make us do the training on these super old tablets with totally shattered screens. My phone screen is actually cracked right now, too. I dropped it in the Target parking lot last week because I was trying to balance my keys and this giant iced coffee at the same time. It was one of those brown sugar oat milk shaken espressos? They are so good, but they're getting ridiculously expensive now. I swear it was almost seven dollars just for a coffee! My roommate makes hers at home with this little frother wand she bought off TikTok shop, but I just don't have the patience to stand there and make it myself in the morning. Plus, I heard TikTok shop is super sketchy anyway, like people get their credit card info stolen on there all the time. I'd rather just go to the drive-thru, even if it costs more. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, focusing on stuff. Yeah, if it's boring like the inventory logs, my brain just kind of checks out completely.
Do you find that you frequently lose things like your keys, wallet, or paperwork, or do you often find yourself becoming easily distracted by things going on around you?

Yeah, the distraction thing is huge. Like, when I'm on the line at work? Literally just one beep from another machine, or if somebody walks past with a pallet jack, my eyes and my whole brain just get completely pulled away from what I'm doing. And I know I'm supposed to just stay on my own station and focus, but I just can't help looking. 

Those pallet jacks are so loud, too. They have these hard wheels that just grind on the concrete all day. My uncle actually used to work in concrete. He poured driveways and patios and stuff, but he messed up his back really bad doing it. He had to get this crazy surgery where they put all these metal screws in his spine. I saw the X-ray on his Facebook once and it literally looked like he swallowed a bunch of hardware from Home Depot. I actually love going to Home Depot, honestly. It always smells so good in there, like fresh sawdust and plants. I bought a little succulent there last month but I already killed it because I kept forgetting to water it. Or maybe I watered it too much? I can never remember what you're supposed to do with those things. People say they're impossible to kill but I guess I proved them wrong. 

But um... wait, what were you asking me? Oh, losing things! Yeah, I mean I do lose my keys all the time, but the distraction thing on the line is definitely the biggest issue.

When you think about the problems you've had at school and work, would you say the bigger issue is that you have trouble focusing and finishing tasks, or is it more that you act without thinking and have trouble staying still?

Honestly, it's definitely the acting without thinking and not being able to sit still. Like, I just feel this constant need to be moving or doing something, and I'll just jump up or blurt something out before my brain even catches up. 

It's kind of like when I go grocery shopping. I'll go in for, like, milk and bread, and then suddenly I'm in the aisle with the baking stuff and I'm throwing three boxes of brownie mix in my cart because I just decided right then that I need to make brownies. Which I never end up doing, by the way. I still have a box of red velvet cake mix in my pantry from like, six months ago. Red velvet is so weird if you think about it. It's just chocolate cake with a ton of red food coloring, right? But people go crazy for it. My sister had a red velvet wedding cake and it was honestly kind of dry. The frosting was good though, it was that cream cheese kind. I could probably just eat a tub of cream cheese frosting with a spoon. 

But um, yeah, definitely the moving around and acting on impulse. The focus thing is bad too, but the physical part of it gets me in trouble way more.
